title: tau explain --json output
description: Schema for the JSON `tau explain [--json]` prints on stdout. With a <code|type|key|doctor.<check>> query the output is a single entry object — an error entry for a code/type query, a config-key entry for a key query (including dotted keys.<provider> member paths), or a doctor-check entry for a `doctor.<check>` or bare check-id query; with no query it is a catalog object {"errors":[entry, ...],"config_keys":[key_entry, ...],"doctor_checks":[check_entry, ...]} holding every entry. Error entries describe one stable exit code: code doubles as the process exit status, type is the wire tag used in err envelopes, cause/hint are informational remediation text (may be reworded), docs is the guide link. Config-key entries mirror one row of the generated docs/config.md table: key is the config-file key, type its JSON type, constraints the constraint cell text, description the key's description, docs the config reference link. Doctor-check entries mirror one row of the generated check table in docs/troubleshooting.md: check is the `tau doctor` report row id, fails_when the condition that warns/fails, remediation the fix, docs the troubleshooting-section link. New keys may be added (additive); existing keys keep their names and types.

code.description: Exit code this entry documents; also the process exit status when the error is raised.

type.description: Wire tag used in the err envelope's "type" field (e.g. "AuthFailed").

recoverable.description: Whether retrying the operation can succeed.

cause.description: One line naming when this error is raised; informational, may be reworded.

hint.description: Remediation hint; informational, may be reworded.

docs.description: Guide link for this error class.

key.description: Config-file key this entry documents — a flat key (e.g. "timeout_ms") or a dotted keys.<provider> member path (e.g. "keys.openai").

type.description: JSON type the config key accepts.

constraints.description: Constraint cell text identical to the generated docs/config.md Constraints column (enum members, ranges, non-empty, member-name rules; "—" when unconstrained); informational, may be reworded.

description.description: One line describing what the key controls; informational, may be reworded.

docs.description: Link to the generated config-key reference (docs/config.md).

check.description: Check id as it appears in the `tau doctor` report's "name" field (e.g. "tls_ca", "client_zed", "probe_openai_auth"); queried as `doctor.<check>` or bare.

fails_when.description: The condition that makes the check warn or fail — the same cell text the generated docs/troubleshooting.md check table renders; informational, may be reworded.

remediation.description: The fix that resolves the check — flag, env var, or command; informational, may be reworded.

docs.description: Link to the doctor-checks section of docs/troubleshooting.md.

errors.description: Every entry in the stable error catalog, ordered by exit code.

config_keys.description: Every resolvable config key — each generated docs/config.md key row plus each keys.<provider> member path.

doctor_checks.description: Every resolvable `tau doctor` check id — each row of the generated docs/troubleshooting.md check table.

examples.cause: the provider rejected the API key, or no key was found anywhere in the resolution chain
examples.hint: provide an API key via --api-key, the provider env var, config.json, or TAU_API_KEY

examples.fails_when: CURL_CA_BUNDLE/SSL_CERT_FILE points at a missing or non-file path, or an SSL_CERT_DIR entry is missing (fail — every HTTPS request would error); a configured proxy with no custom CA bundle warns — the corporate TLS-intercept case (runs under --offline)
examples.remediation: set CURL_CA_BUNDLE (or SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR) to your organization's PEM bundle, or fix/remove the missing path

errors.cause: a named resource is missing — the message identifies the file, skill, or session
errors.hint: the message names what was not found — check the name/path and retry

config_keys.description: Active provider name — selects the API endpoint and default model. TAU_ENDPOINT overrides the endpoint.

doctor_checks.fails_when: CURL_CA_BUNDLE/SSL_CERT_FILE points at a missing or non-file path, or an SSL_CERT_DIR entry is missing (fail — every HTTPS request would error); a configured proxy with no custom CA bundle warns — the corporate TLS-intercept case (runs under --offline)
doctor_checks.remediation: set CURL_CA_BUNDLE (or SSL_CERT_FILE/SSL_CERT_DIR) to your organization's PEM bundle, or fix/remove the missing path
